{
  "subtype": "focus_inference",
  "implied_focus": "Themes/dimensions of student experience with (remote/online) learning as expressed in open responses",
  "per_column": [
    {"name": "tech_experience", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures a technology-related theme (platform/connectivity) students raise about their learning experience."},
    {"name": "pedagogy_quality", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "A coherent theme about instructional quality expressed in responses."},
    {"name": "subject_format_fit", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Theme about how well the subject fits the delivery format."},
    {"name": "student_engagement_level", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Engagement is a distinct experiential theme students raise."},
    {"name": "social_peer_community_loss", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Social/community dimension, a recurring theme in such responses."},
    {"name": "teacher_feedback_responsiveness", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Feedback/responsiveness is a coherent theme facet."},
    {"name": "unexpected_positive_outcome", "supports_focus": true, "rationale": "Captures positive/emergent themes, complementing the negative facets."}
  ],
  "focus_coherence": 0.9,
  "structure_quality": 0.85,
  "focus_actionability": 0.85,
  "rationale": "The added columns collectively centre on one coherent inferred focus: the themes present in students' open responses about their learning experience. Each column is a semantically distinct thematic facet (technology, pedagogy, subject-format fit, engagement, social/community, feedback, positive outcomes), coded with graded categorical values including a 'not_present' option that directly maps to whether a theme is raised -- exactly matching the query about 'what different themes' students raise. This forms a sound multi-facet analytical structure at a useful granularity, neither a single restatement nor generic noise (it avoids trivial text-length/sentiment measures). The facets are non-overlapping and analyst-actionable: one could rank theme prevalence, cross with satisfaction/subject, and investigate drivers. Minor deduction because the facet set is somewhat pre-imposed rather than clearly emergent, and could risk missing some student-raised themes, but overall it strongly realises focus inference."
}
